annotations.title: Interest on damages calculator (special account rate, 2%, 8%)

description: Works out interest on damages before judgment in England and Wales (Senior Courts Act 1981 s.35A; County Courts Act 1984 s.69), head by head: general damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenity at 2% a year from service of the claim form; past losses running to the end date at half the Court Funds Office special account rate from when they began; a loss on one date (a large expense, a bereavement award, funeral costs) at the full rate; a loss that stopped before the end date by one of three methods; and a debt at 8%, another rate or Bank Rate plus a margin, with wording for the particulars of claim (CPR 16.4(2)). Uses every special account rate since 1 February 1993, credits interest on interim payments against the past losses, and gives the daily rate. No interest on future losses. With mode "latePayment" it works out statutory interest on business debts under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 instead: 8% over Bank Rate on the 30 June or 31 December before interest starts, from the day after the agreed or default payment date (s.4), and the £40, £70 or £100 fixed sum for each debt (s.5A).

court.description: County Court (s.69, the default) or High Court (s.35A); only changes the wording for a debt.

debts.description: mode "latePayment" only: the unpaid invoices, each a qualifying debt under a contract for goods or services between businesses (up to 12).

agreed.description: The payment date agreed in the contract, if any (YYYY-MM-DD).

amount.description: The sum due on the invoice, including VAT if VAT was charged (our reading of the Act), in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

label.description: A name for the debt, such as "Invoice 1043".

notice.description: The day the purchaser had notice of the amount, usually the day the invoice was received (YYYY-MM-DD).

performed.description: The day the supplier delivered the goods or finished the services, if later than the notice (YYYY-MM-DD).

verified.description: The day an acceptance or verification procedure was completed, if the contract has one (YYYY-MM-DD).

endDate.description: The date to calculate to: trial, judgment or settlement; for a claim form, the date of issue or earlier (defaults to today) (YYYY-MM-DD).

heads.description: The heads of loss, each worked out on its own.

amount.description: The amount of the head (past losses before deducting recoverable benefits; lost earnings net of tax), in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

from.description: "psla": the date the claim form was served. "continuing" and "ended": the date the loss began. "oneoff": the date it was incurred. "debt": the date it fell due (YYYY-MM-DD).

label.description: A name for the head, such as "Past loss of earnings".

method.description: "ended" only: "midpoint" (the default) for the full rate from the midpoint of the loss; "split" for half the rate while it ran, then the full rate; "half" for half the rate throughout.

rate.description: "debt" only: the fixed rate, or the margin over Bank Rate, in % (e.g. "3.5").

rateKind.description: "debt" only: "statutory" for 8% (the default), "fixed" for the rate in rate, "base" for Bank Rate plus the margin in rate.

to.description: "ended" only: the date the loss stopped (YYYY-MM-DD).

type.description: "psla": general damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenity, 2% from service of the claim form. "continuing": a past loss running to the end date (earnings, care), half the special account rate. "oneoff": a past loss on one date (an expense, bereavement, funeral), the full rate. "ended": a past loss over a period that stopped before the end date. "debt": a debt or other sum at a set rate.

interimPayments.description: Interim payments, each with a date and an amount. Interest on them is credited against the interest on past losses.

amount.description: Amount paid, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

interimRate.description: Credit interest on interim payments at the "full" special account rate (the default) or "half" of it; courts differ.

longTerms.description: mode "latePayment" only, where agreed terms run past 60 days (s.4(2E)) or a 30-day verification period (s.4(5C)): "limit" (the default) applies the limit; "agreed" treats the longer terms as not grossly unfair (s.4(2F), (5D)).

mode.description: "damages" (the default): interest on heads of damages or a debt under s.35A or s.69, using heads. "latePayment": statutory interest and fixed sums on business debts under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998, using debts.

publicAuthority.description: mode "latePayment" only: true if the purchaser is a public authority (s.4(8)), so an agreed date cannot push the start past the 30-day period (s.4(2D)).
